data.title: AXIA Energia Board Approves R$6 Billion PNC Share Redemption
data.description:
An announcement from Centrais Eletricas Brasileiras SA-Eletrobras ( (BR:AXIA3) ) is now available.

AXIA Energia’s board approved the redemption of 129,982,668 Class C preferred shares, valued at R$6.0 billion and representing 49.91% of the remaining shares in that class. The redemption value is R$46.16 per share, based on the closing price of the company’s common shares on November 25, 2026.

Shareholders who do not elect conversion will be automatically redeemed, while PNC holders may convert all or part of eligible shares into common shares at a one-for-one ratio during December 3-7, 2026. ADR holders cannot elect conversion and will have the underlying PNC shares mandatorily redeemed, with proceeds transferred by Citibank N.A.

data.title: AFC reports lower revenue and reduced interim loss
data.description:
AFC Group Holdings Limited ( (NZ:AFC) ) has provided an update.

AFC Group Holdings Limited’s reported revenue comes from cosmetic and wine products, and its businesses include biotechnology manufacturing. Longview Estate maintained vineyard and wine inventories, while AFC Biotechnology Manufacture Co Limited generated limited sales from existing stock and had largely unutilised manufacturing capacity before ceasing operations after the period end.

For the six months ended 30 September 2026, operating revenue was NZ$19,723, down from NZ$33,053, and the net loss was NZ$282,476, compared with NZ$363,640 a year earlier. The group had net liabilities of NZ$76,086, current liabilities exceeding current assets, and a disclosed material uncertainty related to going concern; no dividend was proposed.

data.title: Abcourt Reports First-Quarter Results With C$7.0 Million Gold Revenue
data.description:
Abcourt Mines ( (TSE:ABI) ) has shared an update.

Abcourt Mines, a Canadian gold company developing the Sleeping Giant mine and mill and exploring its Flordin property in northwestern Quebec, reported first-quarter results for the period ended September 30, 2026. It sold 1,155 ounces of gold at an average realized price of C$5,848 per ounce, generating C$7.0 million in revenue, compared with no revenue in the year-earlier quarter.

Costs of sales were C$16.8 million and net loss was C$13.2 million, compared with a C$7.5 million loss in the prior-year quarter. Abcourt increased its Glencore senior secured debenture to US$40 million, had drawn US$38 million by September 30, and repaid its Nebari facility in full in September; cash was C$1.4 million and working capital was C$1.9 million at quarter-end.

data.title: New Zealand Consumer Confidence Surges Past Expectations
data.description:
New Zealand’s ANZ Roy Morgan Consumer Confidence rose to 100.2 from 96.2, an increase of 4.0 points, or about 4.2%. The reading moved higher and returned above the 100 threshold.

The result exceeded the analyst estimate of 96.5 by 3.7 points, or about 3.8%, signaling firmer consumer sentiment than expected. Retailers and consumer-discretionary stocks are likely to benefit from improved demand expectations, while the broader market impact should be short-term and sentiment-driven.

data.title: ARSESP Validates Sabesp’s 2025 Regulatory Asset Base at R$97.8 Billion
data.description:
Companhia de Saneamento Basico do Estado de Sao Paulo SABESP ( (BR:SBSP3) ) just unveiled an announcement.

Sabesp said São Paulo’s public-services regulator, ARSESP, validated its 2025 Regulatory Asset Base at R$97.8 billion, measured at December 2025 values. The figure rose from a protected RAB of R$88.0 billion at December 2024, incorporating R$10.9 billion in gross additions, R$4.0 billion of inflation and R$3.8 billion in depreciation.

Other adjustments included R$0.6 billion in asset write-offs, R$0.2 billion in photovoltaic solar investments and R$0.3 billion representing the difference between JOA and JOAR. Sabesp said the written-off assets had been in service but were no longer operating, while the solar investments were not recognized in the 2024 and 2025 RAB.
